contents.name: Section 3.1 Eqs. (3.1)-(3.4): the particle on a line with L = m xdot^2/2 - U(x,t), the equation m xddot = -dU/dx, and the effectively one-dimensional class with effective mass m_ef and effective potential U_ef

Section 3.2 Eqs. (3.8)-(3.12): the fixed-point condition dU_ef/dq = 0, the Taylor expansion about a fixed point and the effective spring constant kappa_ef = d^2U_ef/dq^2, with the linearised equation m_ef qddot = -kappa_ef q

Section 3.2 Eqs. (3.15)-(3.18): harmonic oscillations with frequency (kappa_ef/m_ef)^{1/2} at a minimum, the exponentially growing solution at a maximum, and the equivalence with the linearised force F_ef = -kappa_ef q
Section 3.3 Eqs. (3.24)-(3.29): the energy as a first integral of the one-dimensional motion, the energy diagram, turning points and the period as twice the quadrature between turning points
Section 5.1 Eqs. (5.1)-(5.2): the harmonic oscillator Lagrangian and equation m qddot + kappa q = 0 with omega_0 = (kappa/m)^{1/2}
Section 5.1 Eqs. (5.3a)-(5.4): the general solution u cos(omega_0 t) + v sin(omega_0 t) = A cos(omega_0 t - phi), amplitude and phase, and the conserved energy E = kappa A^2/2

Section 5.1 Eqs. (5.5)-(5.6b) with footnote 4: the linear drag force F = -eta qdot, the damped equation m qddot + eta qdot + kappa q = 0, and the phenomenological status of the drag with its neglected random component
Section 5.1 Eqs. (5.6)-(5.12): the characteristic equation and its roots, the free solution, the exponential decay with time constant 1/delta, the quality factor and the energy-decay relation
Section 5.1 Eqs. (5.9)-(5.12) and footnote 5: the three damping regimes, the decay of free oscillations and the two relaxation time scales in the heavily damped limit
Section 5.1 Eqs. (5.13a)-(5.19): the forced equation m qddot + eta qdot + kappa q = F(t), the response function, the forced amplitude and the resonance value
Section 5.1 Eqs. (5.14)-(5.22): the forced-oscillation solution as free plus forced parts, the amplitude (5.18), the resonance value (5.19) and the half width of the resonance curve
Sections 5.2-5.3: weakly nonlinear oscillations, secular terms and Duffing harmonic balance
contents.reason: Nonlinear oscillation theory belongs to the coupled-oscillation and stability pages of the track (CM09/CM16); this page states and proves only the linear models' exact motion theory.
